answers.q1: After the first 5 seconds I think it is a coin game where one player ends up with 90% of the money, and the video will show how that happens. The thumbnail (gold coin tower, king in a green cone hat, FAIR GAME?) and the title (one winner, every time) match. I got the 'fair game with one winner' idea clearly.
answers.q2: Partly. 'Nobody cheated' and 'he is not smarter' make me curious, and the 1% line gives a real-world reason to care. But the reason to care is only clear around the 1% line, and before that it is a mystery without stakes for me.
answers.q3: Yes, roughly: they will test a fair coin game with four players who get advantages (Scholar, Worker, Heir, Fool), run it 10,000 times, and then show a rule that stops the king. The 'one rule' is a promise I like, but I would not know what the rule is for.
answers.q4: Most likely around the 'Pick your winner now' line (line 22). I am asked to pick a winner before I know the game, the four characters or what the 'winner' means, so it feels like I am being told to do something I cannot do yet. Also the long run of character intros (lines 45 to 64) with 'for now the hats mean nothing' could make me leave: four pawns, a name each, and no game yet. I might leave around the 'Here is the whole game' moment, wondering how long until it starts.
answers.q5:
'Some of you will hate who wins.' Sounds like a dare and a bit preachy. Better: 'Pick the one you think will win.'

'For now the hats mean nothing... but keep an eye on them.' Filler-ish. Better: 'The hats will matter. Watch what they do.'

'This game says something they will hate: being rich does not prove you were better.' Preachy for a coin video before I see the game. Better: 'In a fair game, does being rich mean you were better? Let's test it.'

'Because nobody can bet what they don't have.' Fine, but 'both risk the same amount' needs one more beat: 'Both put in 20 coins, so the risk is equal, even though one has four times more.'
answers.q6: I would comment only if the game shows something surprising. Right now I would type 'wait, which hat wins?' or 'so is the coin fair or not?' I would not type anything yet in the first 100 seconds.

gap_to_gate.line: Pick your winner now. Some of you will hate who wins.
gap_to_gate.problem: I am asked to pick a winner before I know the game, the four characters or the rules. Sounds like a dare, and 'hate' feels preachy.
gap_to_gate.fix_wording: Before the game starts, who do you think wins a fair coin game? Pick one of the four.

gap_to_gate.line: This game says something they will hate: being rich does not prove you were better.
gap_to_gate.problem: Preachy and political before I know the game. It tells me what to think instead of letting me test it.
gap_to_gate.fix_wording: In a fair game, does being rich mean you were better? Let's test it.

gap_to_gate.line: For now the hats mean nothing. All four play by exactly the same rules as everyone else. But keep an eye on them.
gap_to_gate.problem: Filler: four characters and no game yet, so the setup drags. I do not know what the hats will do or why I should watch.
gap_to_gate.fix_wording: The hats are the only difference. Watch what they do to the coin.

gap_to_gate.line: Here is the whole game. (then 'Two players are picked at random...')
gap_to_gate.problem: Setup runs about 60 seconds before the rules appear. A stranger may leave before the game starts.
gap_to_gate.fix_wording: Here is the game in 10 seconds: a coin flip, a bet, and one winner takes all. Then the four hats join.

gap_to_gate.line: Both risk the same amount. That is as fair as a bet gets.
gap_to_gate.problem: Confusing: the 100-coin player risks a bigger share of his money than the 400-coin player, so 'same amount' does not feel fair to me right away.
gap_to_gate.fix_wording: Both put in 20 coins, so the risk is equal to each player. The poorer player is not punished, and the richer one cannot cheat the bet.
